source.text: concilium rex triste vocat, quaeruntque gementes, quis tripodas successor agat, quo provida laurus transeat atque orbum vittae decus, haud mora, cuncti insignem fama sancteque Melampode cretum Thiodamanta volunt, quicum ipse arcana deorum partiri et visas uni sociare solebat Amphiaraus aves, tantaeque haud invidus artis gaudebat dici similem iuxtaque secundum, illum ingens confundit honos inopinaque turbat gloria et oblatas frondes submissus adorat, seque oneri negat esse parem cogique meretur:
source.text_original: concilium rex triste vocat, quaeruntque gementes, / quis tripodas successor agat, quo provida laurus / transeat atque orbum vittae decus, haud mora, cuncti / insignem fama sancteque Melampode cretum / Thiodamanta volunt, quicum ipse arcana deorum / partiri et visas uni sociare solebat / Amphiaraus aves, tantaeque haud invidus artis / gaudebat dici similem iuxtaque secundum, / illum ingens confundit honos inopinaque turbat / gloria et oblatas frondes submissus adorat, / seque oneri negat esse parem cogique meretur: /
source.text_english: The king summons a sorrowful council, and the mourners ask who should take up the tripod in succession, to whom the prudent laurel should pass and the wreath’s honor, now bereft, No delay: all want Thiodamas, renowned in fame and born of holy Melampus, with whom Amphiaraus himself used to share the secret counsels of the gods and to join in fellowship the birds he alone had seen. He did not begrudge such skill, and rejoiced to be called his equal and next in rank. Great honor and unexpected glory overwhelm him, and bowing low he worships the laurel branches offered to him, and says he is not equal to the burden and deserves to be compelled:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Protinus Inachiis ultro Tirynthius Argis advolat, Arcadio cuius flammata veneno tela puer facilesque umeris gaudentibus arcus gestat Hylas: velit ille quidem, sed dextera nondum par oneri clavaeque capax.
reuse.text_original: Protinus Inachiis ultro Tirynthius Argis / advolat, Arcadio cuius flammata veneno / tela puer facilesque umeris gaudentibus arcus / gestat Hylas: velit ille quidem, sed dextera nondum / par oneri clavaeque capax.
reuse.text_english: Straightway the Tirynthian flies of his own accord to Argos of Inachus, where Hylas carries for him the poisoned darts and the bows that delight his eager shoulders—Arcadian weapons: he would indeed wish it, but his right hand is not yet equal to the burden, nor able to bear the club.
